subject: B
topic: Popular Names of Personalities (Religion, Politics, Science, Sports)

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who is popularly known as the 'Father of the Nation' in India?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi is called the 'Father of the Nation' for leading India's freedom struggle through non-violence. Jawaharlal Nehru is wrong — he is known as 'Chacha Nehru' and the architect of modern India. Sardar Patel is wrong — he is called the 'Iron Man of India'. B.R. Ambedkar is wrong — he is known as the 'Father of the Indian Constitution'.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about popular names of Indian political personalities:

(i) Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel is called the 'Iron Man of India'.
(ii) Subhas Chandra Bose is called 'Netaji'.
(iii) Jawaharlal Nehru is called 'Deshbandhu'.
(iv) Lal Bahadur Shastri gave the slogan 'Jai Jawan Jai Kisan'.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Sardar Patel is called the Iron Man for his role in integrating 562 princely states into India. (ii) is correct — Subhas Chandra Bose was respectfully called 'Netaji' (respected leader). (iv) is correct — Lal Bahadur Shastri coined 'Jai Jawan Jai Kisan' during the 1965 war. (iii) is wrong — 'Deshbandhu' (Friend of the Nation) was the title of Chittaranjan Das, not Nehru. Nehru was called 'Pandit Nehru' and 'Chacha Nehru'.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who is known as the 'Missile Man of India'?
questions.explanation: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam is called the 'Missile Man of India' for his pivotal role in developing India's ballistic missile and space programmes (Agni, Prithvi). Vikram Sarabhai is wrong — he is called the 'Father of the Indian Space Programme'. Homi J. Bhabha is wrong — he is the 'Father of India's Nuclear Programme'. Satish Dhawan is wrong — he is known as the 'Father of Experimental Fluid Dynamics' in India.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): B.R. Ambedkar is called the 'Father of the Indian Constitution'.
Reason (R): He was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly and played the key role in framing the Indian Constitution.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Ambedkar is revered as the Father of the Indian Constitution. Reason (R) is also correct — he chaired the Drafting Committee and was the principal architect of the Constitution. (R) explains (A) because his leading role in drafting is exactly why he received this title. Option 2 is wrong because (R) directly explains (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is historically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following personalities with their popular names/titles:

Column I:
(a) Swami Vivekananda
(b) Rabindranath Tagore
(c) C.V. Raman
(d) Madan Mohan Malaviya

Column II:
(i) Mahamana
(ii) Gurudev
(iii) The Monk Who Shook the World at Chicago
(iv) Nobel Laureate in Physics (first Indian)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Swami Vivekananda is famous for his 1893 Chicago speech — matches (iii). (b) Rabindranath Tagore was called 'Gurudev' (divine teacher) — matches (ii). (c) C.V. Raman was the first Indian to win the Nobel Prize in Physics (1930) — matches (iv). (d) Madan Mohan Malaviya was given the title 'Mahamana' (great soul) — matches (i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly matched with their popular names?

(i) Sachin Tendulkar — 'God of Cricket'
(ii) Milkha Singh — 'Flying Sikh'
(iii) P.T. Usha — 'Payyoli Express'
(iv) Kapil Dev — 'Wall of India'

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Sachin Tendulkar is called the 'God of Cricket' or 'Master Blaster'. (ii) is correct — Milkha Singh earned the nickname 'Flying Sikh' for his incredible speed. (iii) is correct — P.T. Usha from Payyoli, Kerala is called the 'Payyoli Express'. (iv) is wrong — 'Wall of India' is the nickname of Rahul Dravid, not Kapil Dev. Kapil Dev is called 'Haryana Hurricane'.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who is known as the 'Lady with the Lamp'?
questions.explanation: Florence Nightingale (1820–1910) is called the 'Lady with the Lamp' for tending to wounded soldiers at night during the Crimean War, earning her this symbolic title. Mother Teresa is wrong — she is called the 'Saint of the Gutters' or 'Angel of Mercy'. Marie Curie is wrong — she is known for discovering radium, not nursing. Indira Gandhi is wrong — she was India's PM, called the 'Iron Lady of India'.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about sobriquet names in Indian politics:

(i) Bal Gangadhar Tilak was called 'Lokmanya' (Accepted by the people).
(ii) Lala Lajpat Rai was called 'Punjab Kesari' (Lion of Punjab).
(iii) Bipin Chandra Pal was called the 'Father of Indian Unrest'.
(iv) Gopal Krishna Gokhale was called 'the political guru of Gandhi'.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Tilak earned 'Lokmanya' for his popularity among the masses. (ii) is correct — Lala Lajpat Rai was called 'Punjab Kesari' for his lion-like leadership. (iv) is correct — Gandhi himself regarded Gokhale as his political guru. (iii) is wrong — 'Father of Indian Unrest' was the title given to Bal Gangadhar TILAK by the British journalist Valentine Chirol, not Bipin Chandra Pal.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: Vikram Sarabhai is popularly known as the 'Father of __________'.
questions.explanation: Vikram Sarabhai is called the 'Father of the Indian Space Programme' for establishing ISRO and laying the foundation for India's space research. 'Indian Nuclear Programme' is wrong — that title belongs to Homi J. Bhabha. 'Indian Missile Programme' is wrong — that is associated with A.P.J. Abdul Kalam. 'Indian Computer Science' is wrong — no such widely recognized title is associated with Sarabhai.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Milkha Singh was called the 'Flying Sikh'.
Reason (R): He ran barefoot in international competitions and narrowly missed an Olympic medal in the 400m at the 1960 Rome Olympics, earning global recognition for his extraordinary speed.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Milkha Singh was famously called the 'Flying Sikh'. Reason (R) is also correct — his incredible speed, especially at the 1960 Rome Olympics where he finished 4th in 400m by a whisker, earned him this name. (R) explains (A) because his remarkable athletic performances are what led to the nickname. Option 2 is wrong because (R) provides the reason for the title. Option 3 is wrong because (R) is historically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who is known as the 'Grand Old Man of India'?
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji (1825–1917) is called the 'Grand Old Man of India' for his long service to the nation and his role in the early Indian National Congress. Mahatma Gandhi is wrong — he is the 'Father of the Nation'. Rajendra Prasad is wrong — he was the first President of India. W.C. Bonnerjee is wrong — he was the first Congress president but not known by this title.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following sports personalities with their nicknames:

Column I:
(a) Rahul Dravid
(b) Virender Sehwag
(c) M.S. Dhoni
(d) Sunil Gavaskar

Column II:
(i) Little Master
(ii) Captain Cool
(iii) Nawab of Najafgarh
(iv) The Wall

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Rahul Dravid = 'The Wall' for his solid, dependable batting — matches (iv). (b) Virender Sehwag = 'Nawab of Najafgarh' (his birthplace in Delhi) — matches (iii). (c) M.S. Dhoni = 'Captain Cool' for his calm demeanour under pressure — matches (ii). (d) Sunil Gavaskar = 'Little Master' for his short stature and masterful batting — matches (i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Swami Vivekananda's real name was:
questions.explanation: Swami Vivekananda's birth name was Narendranath Datta (1863–1902). Gadadhar Chattopadhyay is wrong — that was the birth name of Ramakrishna Paramhansa. Mool Shankar Tiwari is wrong — that was the birth name of Swami Dayanand Saraswati. Vishwanath Dutta is wrong — that was Vivekananda's father, not his own name.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about religious reformers and their titles:

(i) Raja Ram Mohan Roy is called the 'Father of the Indian Renaissance'.
(ii) Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj.
(iii) Guru Nanak Dev is the founder of Sikhism.
(iv) Ramakrishna Paramhansa founded the Ramakrishna Mission.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Raja Ram Mohan Roy (1772–1833) is called the Father of the Indian Renaissance for his social reforms and founding of Brahmo Samaj. (ii) is correct — Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in 1875. (iii) is correct — Guru Nanak Dev (1469–1539) founded Sikhism. (iv) is wrong — Ramakrishna Mission was founded by Swami VIVEKANANDA in 1897, not by Ramakrishna Paramhansa (who was Vivekananda's guru).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who is popularly known as the 'Iron Lady of India'?
questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi was called the 'Iron Lady of India' for her strong and decisive political leadership. Sarojini Naidu is wrong — she was called the 'Nightingale of India'. Sucheta Kripalani is wrong — she was the first woman Chief Minister of an Indian state (UP). Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit is wrong — she was the first woman President of the UN General Assembly.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Sarojini Naidu is called the 'Nightingale of India'.
Reason (R): She was a celebrated poet whose lyrical verses in English were admired for their beauty and melody.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Sarojini Naidu (1879–1949) is called the 'Nightingale of India'. Reason (R) is also correct — her poetry collections like 'The Golden Threshold' and 'The Bird of Time' are admired for lyrical beauty. (R) explains (A) because her melodious poetry (like a nightingale's song) earned her this title. Option 2 is wrong because (R) directly explains (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is factually correct. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who is known as the 'Father of the Indian Constitution'?
questions.explanation: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar is known as the Father of the Indian Constitution as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee. Jawaharlal Nehru is wrong — he moved the Objectives Resolution but was not the chief architect of the Constitution. Rajendra Prasad is wrong — he was the President of the Constituent Assembly but not the drafter. Sardar Patel is wrong — he handled states' integration, not the Constitution drafting.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly matched?

(i) 'Frontier Gandhi' — Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan
(ii) 'Gurudev' — Rabindranath Tagore
(iii) 'Lokpriya' — Gopinath Bordoloi
(iv) 'Deshbandhu' — Motilal Nehru

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (Badshah Khan) was called 'Frontier Gandhi' for his non-violent movement in the North-West Frontier. (ii) is correct — Tagore was called 'Gurudev' by his admirers. (iii) is correct — Gopinath Bordoloi was called 'Lokpriya' (Beloved of the People) in Assam. (iv) is wrong — 'Deshbandhu' was the title of Chittaranjan Das, not Motilal Nehru.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following scientists with their popular titles:

Column I:
(a) Homi J. Bhabha
(b) M. Visvesvaraya
(c) Srinivasa Ramanujan
(d) Jagadish Chandra Bose

Column II:
(i) Father of Indian Engineering
(ii) Father of Indian Nuclear Programme
(iii) Mathematical genius / 'Man Who Knew Infinity'
(iv) Father of Radio Science in India

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Homi J. Bhabha = Father of Indian Nuclear Programme — matches (ii). (b) M. Visvesvaraya = Father of Indian Engineering (Engineer's Day celebrated on his birthday, 15 Sept) — matches (i). (c) Srinivasa Ramanujan = Mathematical genius known as 'The Man Who Knew Infinity' — matches (iii). (d) J.C. Bose = Pioneer of radio science / wireless communication research — matches (iv). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (d). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who is known as the 'Indian Napoleon'?
questions.explanation: Samudragupta (c. 335–375 AD) is called the 'Indian Napoleon' by historian V.A. Smith for his extensive military conquests across India. Chandragupta Maurya is wrong — he is known as the founder of the Maurya Empire. Ashoka is wrong — he is known as 'Ashoka the Great' and promoter of Buddhism and peace. Akbar is wrong — he is called 'Akbar the Great' for his administrative and cultural achievements.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about sporting personalities and their nicknames:

(i) Usain Bolt is called 'Lightning Bolt'.
(ii) Pelé is called the 'King of Football'.
(iii) Muhammad Ali called himself 'The Greatest'.
(iv) Don Bradman is called the 'Flying Dutchman'.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Usain Bolt's nickname 'Lightning Bolt' suits his world-record sprinting speed. (ii) is correct — Pelé (Brazil) is universally called the King of Football. (iii) is correct — Muhammad Ali famously proclaimed himself 'The Greatest' throughout his boxing career. (iv) is wrong — 'Flying Dutchman' is not Don Bradman's nickname; Bradman is called 'The Don'. 'Flying Dutchman' is associated with Dutch athletes.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The title 'Mahatma' was given to Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi by:
questions.explanation: The title 'Mahatma' (Great Soul) is widely attributed to Rabindranath Tagore, who used it for Gandhi. Subhas Chandra Bose is wrong — he gave Gandhi the title 'Father of the Nation'. Jawaharlal Nehru is wrong — he did not coin this title. Gopal Krishna Gokhale is wrong — he was Gandhi's political mentor but did not bestow this title.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who is known as the 'Bharat Kokila' (Nightingale of India)?
questions.explanation: Sarojini Naidu is called 'Bharat Kokila' (Nightingale of India) for her melodious poetry. Lata Mangeshkar is wrong — she was called the 'Nightingale of Bollywood' or 'Queen of Melody', which is different from Bharat Kokila. M.S. Subbulakshmi is wrong — she was called the 'Queen of Music' (Carnatic). Begum Akhtar is wrong — she was called the 'Queen of Ghazals'.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following table shows popular names and the number of personalities associated with each field:

Freedom Fighters → 12
Scientists → 6
Sports → 8
Religious Leaders → 4

What percentage of the total titled personalities are from the Sports field?
questions.explanation: Total = 12 + 6 + 8 + 4 = 30. Sports percentage = (8/30) × 100 = 26.67%. 25% is wrong — would mean 7.5 out of 30. 30% is wrong — would mean 9 out of 30. 20% is wrong — would mean 6 out of 30.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who among the following is known as 'Lokmanya'?
questions.explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak (1856–1920) was called 'Lokmanya' (Accepted/Revered by the People) for his mass appeal and nationalist activities. Gopal Krishna Gokhale is wrong — he was called a 'moderate' leader and Gandhi's political guru. Dadabhai Naoroji is wrong — he was called the 'Grand Old Man of India'. Bipin Chandra Pal is wrong — he was part of the 'Lal-Bal-Pal' trio but didn't have the Lokmanya title.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about 'Fathers' in various fields:

(i) Verghese Kurien is called the 'Father of the White Revolution' (milk).
(ii) M.S. Swaminathan is called the 'Father of the Green Revolution in India'.
(iii) Sam Manekshaw is called the 'Father of the Indian Army'.
(iv) Dhirubhai Ambani is called the 'Father of Indian Industry'.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Verghese Kurien led Operation Flood and is called the Father of the White Revolution. (ii) is correct — M.S. Swaminathan pioneered high-yielding crop varieties and is the Father of India's Green Revolution. (iii) is wrong — Sam Manekshaw was a legendary Field Marshal but is not called the 'Father of the Indian Army'. (iv) is wrong — while Dhirubhai Ambani founded Reliance, 'Father of Indian Industry' is not his widely recognized title; J.N. Tata is more closely associated with pioneering Indian industry.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who is known as 'Chacha Nehru' (Uncle Nehru)?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru is lovingly called 'Chacha Nehru' by children because of his great affection for them; his birthday (14 November) is celebrated as Children's Day. Motilal Nehru is wrong — he was Jawaharlal's father, a senior Congress leader. B.K. Nehru is wrong — he was a diplomat/administrator. R.K. Nehru is wrong — he was a civil servant.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following personalities are correctly associated with their fields?

(i) Mother Teresa — Social Service (Saint of the Gutters)
(ii) Dhyan Chand — Hockey (Wizard of Hockey)
(iii) Tansen — Music (one of Akbar's Navratnas)
(iv) Aryabhata — Architecture (designed Red Fort)

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Mother Teresa (now Saint Teresa of Calcutta) served the poorest and is called the Saint of the Gutters. (ii) is correct — Major Dhyan Chand is the Wizard of Hockey. (iii) is correct — Tansen was one of Emperor Akbar's nine gems (Navratnas) in music. (iv) is wrong — Aryabhata was a mathematician and astronomer (5th century), not an architect. The Red Fort was designed by Ustad Ahmad Lahori during Shah Jahan's reign.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who is known as the 'Light of Asia'?
questions.explanation: Gautama Buddha is called the 'Light of Asia' — this title was popularized by Sir Edwin Arnold's 1879 poem of the same name about Buddha's life. Swami Vivekananda is wrong — he is associated with the Chicago address but not this title. Ashoka the Great is wrong — he spread Buddhism but is not himself called 'Light of Asia'. Mahavira is wrong — he is the founder of Jainism.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following world personalities with their popular names:

Column I:
(a) Abraham Lincoln
(b) Napoleon Bonaparte
(c) Adolf Hitler
(d) Nelson Mandela

Column II:
(i) Madiba
(ii) The Great Emancipator
(iii) The Little Corporal
(iv) Führer

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Abraham Lincoln = 'The Great Emancipator' for abolishing slavery — matches (ii). (b) Napoleon = 'The Little Corporal' for his short stature and military rank origin — matches (iii). (c) Adolf Hitler = 'Führer' (Leader), his self-given title in Nazi Germany — matches (iv). (d) Nelson Mandela = 'Madiba', his Xhosa clan name used affectionately — matches (i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).
